title: L1-L5 moment-rotation curves and ROM at 7.5 Nm, 10 intact specimens (Rohlmann 2001b, via Dreischarf 2014)

quantity.name: moment-rotation curve
quantity.definition: L1-L5 (total of 4 segments) rotation vs pure moment, ONE direction from the unloaded position (Fig 2b): median curve of 10 specimens at 1-7 Nm, and at 7.5 Nm the median with the specimen range (min-max). Rows x = *_total are Fig 2a: rotation SUMMED over both directions at +/-7.5 Nm (median and range of the 10 summed values). Rotations stored as positive magnitudes (Dreischarf plots extension and axial rotation negative, lateral bending on the negative-moment side).

source.authors: Rohlmann A, Neller S, Claes L, Bergmann G, Wilke HJ
source.sample: 10 human cadaveric L1-L5 lumbar spines (primary: Rohlmann et al. 2001, 'Influence of a follower load on intradiscal pressure and intersegmental rotation of the lumbar spine'; cited as Rohlmann et al. 2001b by Dreischarf 2014). Primary PDF not on disk: values read from the re-plot in Dreischarf 2014 Fig 2a/2b.

secondary_source.authors: Dreischarf M, Zander T, Shirazi-Adl A, Puttlitz CM, Adam CJ, Chen CS, Goel VK, Kiapour A, Kim YH, Labus KM, Little JP, Park WM, Wang YH, Wilke HJ, Rohlmann A, Schmidt H
secondary_source.where: Fig 2a (red bars) and Fig 2b (black dotted median curves, black markers and red ranges at 7.5 Nm)

protocol.summary: Pure moments up to 7.5 Nm in flexion, extension, lateral bending and axial rotation, no preload (the in vitro reference Dreischarf 2014 used for its pure-moment comparison, Wilke 1998 recommendations); L1-L5 rotation. Rate, cycles and which loading cycle was evaluated are not restated in Dreischarf 2014 (see the primary).
how_to_simulate: Model the L1-L5 osseoligamentous spine; fix L5 (all DOF), apply an unconstrained pure moment to L1, no preload
Step the moment 0-7.5 Nm in flexion, extension, one-sided lateral bending and one-sided axial rotation
Report L1-L5 rotation (one direction, from the unloaded position) at each moment; compare the 7.5 Nm value with the specimen range
For the *_total rows sum both directions (flexion+extension, left+right LB, left+right AR) at +/-7.5 Nm
protocol.notes: Secondary data (re-plot). Direction check: Fig 2b is one direction per quadrant (flexion, extension, one LB side, one AR side); Fig 2a is the summed range (caption: 'L1-5 range of motion'; text: 'flexion-extension', 'left-right lateral bending', 'left-right axial rotation'). LB sum 34.1 ~ 2 x 17.1; FE sum 31.2 vs 21.1+9.3 = 30.4 (median of sums need not equal sum of medians). The in vitro curves rise steeply at small moments (neutral zone included; the flexion and lateral-bending medians already read ~4-5 deg at 0.25-0.35 Nm), so points below 1 Nm are not given. Fig 2 of the on-disk author version (QUT eprints) is one embedded bitmap of 552x415 px for all four panels (Fig 2b plot area 208x123 px: 13 px per Nm, 2.248 px per deg). The image was read at its native pixels (pdfimages, lossless PNG); rendering the page at >=300 dpi only up-samples this bitmap and adds no detail.

extraction.from: Dreischarf 2014 Fig 2a (red bars) and Fig 2b (black dotted median curves; black markers + red ranges at 7.5 Nm)
extraction.uncertainty: +/-0.5 deg for the 7.5 Nm markers and red-bar ends (1 px = 0.44 deg); +/-1 deg for curve points >= 2.5 Nm; +/-1.5 deg for extension and axial-rotation points below 2.5 Nm (dotted median overlaps the grey Model 7 curve there); Fig 2a totals +/-1 deg (1 px = 0.41 deg)
extraction.check_notes: Calibration: Fig 2b frame cols 324/428/532 = -8/0/+8 Nm (13 px/Nm), rows 30.5 = 30 deg, 98 = 0, gridlines every 11.24 px = 5 deg. Every pixel unmixed against the legend colours (alpha + residual); the grey pixels (dotted in vitro median and solid Model 7 share one colour) split into two chains by continuity and by the dot pattern (alternating intensities = dotted), then fitted with a(1-exp(-bM))+cM (rms 0.3-0.4 deg); the lateral-bending median read chain by chain. 7.5 Nm re-read from the markers/caps: flexion 21.1 [17.8, 24.5], LB 17.1 [12.0, 22.6], extension 9.3 [6.0, 12.5], AR 6.45 [4.9, 9.2] - the stored values are those of the earlier verified secondary test (differences <= 0.2 deg). Agreement with the earlier independent digitisation (fe_model_comparison.dreischarf2014.L1L5_invitro_curve_secondary, flexion and LB only): flexion 1-7 Nm within 0.4 deg, LB within 0.3 deg. Extension and AR curves are new (earlier test gave only 7.5 Nm): extension median chain identified as the dotted, concave curve that ends at the 7.5 Nm marker; the straight grey line below it at low moments is Model 7 (its 7.5 Nm values reproduce the Model 7 bars of Fig 2a). Fig 2a totals re-checked: bar tops at rows 77/70/125 -> 31.1/34.0/11.5 deg (stored 31.2/34.1/11.5). Owner targets (fe.json): 'lumbar.L1L5.flex.7p5.rohlmann2001' 21.3 [17.6, 24.8] = this 21.1 [17.8, 24.4] within 0.4 deg (same re-plot, read from Ghezelbash 2024 Fig 2b). Corridor checks: the UPPER dashed curve of Ghezelbash 2024 Fig 2b (16.67 at 2.5 Nm, 20.55 at 5 Nm) is this median curve (16.9, 20.1); the LOWER dashed curve (11.51 at 2.5 Nm, 18.44 at 5 Nm; starts at 0 and is S-shaped) is NOT in Dreischarf 2014 - its source cannot be checked without the primary (maybe another condition of Rohlmann 2001), so the owner's 'corridor' is not a specimen range.

pass_rule.rule: 7.5 Nm: min <= model <= max (specimen range); curve: >= 80% of points within +/-2 deg of the median curve (template); *_total rows: min <= model <= max
